subject: Re: Clarify streaming billing for partial generations & disconnects
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Platform SRE <platform-sre@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2025-09-10T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Rate card + streaming billing question

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re doing well. We’re evaluating Redwood for a user-facing feature that will heavily use streaming text responses (progressive UI -- tokens arrive as the model generates). Before we proceed I need to get a clear read on a couple of billing behaviors so I can model costs:

1) If a client disconnects mid-stream (network blip or user navigates away), are we billed for the tokens the model generated up to the point of disconnect?
2) If the client retries and requests the same prompt again, will we be billed twice for overlapping/generated tokens?
3) Do you have a recommended pattern to minimize double-billing for common retry scenarios?

Could you also send the updated hosted API rate card? We’ll share it with finance for baseline pricing and discounts.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Product Manager
Acme Corp

P.S. We may need a small pilot/commit if the numbers look right.

Subject: Re: Rate card + streaming billing question

On Wed, Sep 10, 2025 at 2:05 PM Jordan Miller <jordan@acmecorp.com> wrote:
> Hi Marissa,
> 
> Hope you’re doing well. We’re evaluating Redwood for a user-facing feature that will heavily use streaming text responses (progressive UI -- tokens arrive as the model generates). Before we proceed I need to get a clear read on a couple of billing behaviors so I can model costs:
> 
> 1) If a client disconnects mid-stream (network blip or user navigates away), are we billed for the tokens the model generated up to the point of disconnect?
> 2) If the client retries and requests the same prompt again, will we be billed twice for overlapping/generated tokens?
> 3) Do you have a recommended pattern to minimize double-billing for common retry scenarios?
> 
> Could you also send the updated hosted API rate card? We’ll share it with finance for baseline pricing and discounts.

Thanks for the clear questions — short answers first, then examples and recommended mitigations below. I attached our current rate card (redwood-ratecard-2025.pdf).

Short answers:
- Disconnects: billed for the tokens the service generated (server-side), even if the client never received the final bytes. The model execution and GPU cycles were consumed.
- Retries: if you re-issue the same generate call and the model produces tokens again, those tokens are billed again. There’s no implicit automatic de-duplication on repeated requests.
- Minimizing double-billing: we recommend idempotency keys and a short server-side generation TTL combined with client-side resume logic, or using non-streaming calls for workflows where exact single-charge semantics are critical.

Details and examples (useful for modeling):
1) Client disconnect mid-stream
   - Scenario: client requests a 512-token generation, server streams tokens as they are produced. Client loses connection after 120 tokens were generated.
   - Billing: Redwood bills for the 120 generated tokens. The server completed generation work for those tokens.

2) Client retry immediately (simple re-call)
   - Scenario: client retries by resending the same prompt. Server will generate a new sequence; if it produces similar output, you will be billed for a second set of tokens.
   - Billing: double-billing of overlapping tokens is possible.

3) Helpful patterns to avoid unnecessary cost
   - Idempotency keys: attach a unique id for each user prompt so your backend can detect retries and serve cached results (or mark the original request as in-progress).
   - Response caching: store the final output for common prompts and return cached copies on retry. Redwood’s caching hooks can be configured to persist short-lived prefixes.
   - Shorten server-side max tokens: set a conservative max_tokens if the UI does not require full-length completion in case of frequent disconnects.
   - Use non-streaming / synchronous calls for short prompts where you need single-charge guarantees; streaming is better when you prioritize latency and UX.

We’re happy to run a short pilot to exercise your retry patterns and measure token usage empirically. Diego is copied to help map the pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-ratecard-2025.pdf (see pricing tables and streaming notes)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from our engineering team:

- If we implement idempotency at our edge, can Redwood surface a short-lived request id or receipt we can use to correlate with billing events in your console? That would let us reconcile automated retries.
- For the pilot: we’ll run a simulation where ~10k prompts/day stream and ~8% of sessions are expected to disconnect mid-stream. Can you give an order-of-magnitude cost delta between streaming with naive retries vs. a cached+idempotent approach? A ballpark number is fine — our finance just needs a modeling delta to evaluate the pilot.

Also cc’ing our Platform SRE (platform-sre@acmecorp.com) — they’ll want to review any limits or throttling behavior that could impact UX.

Appreciate it,
Jordan
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-11T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Rate card + streaming billing question — pilot numbers and discounts

Jordan — looping in finance/plans guidance quickly. We reviewed the numbers and sketched two baseline scenarios for your pilot (estimates only):

Assumptions:
- 10k prompts/day, avg generated length per successful session: 300 tokens.
- Disconnect rate: 8% (these generate on average 120 tokens before drop).
- Your account is evaluating a 3-month pilot.

Scenario A — naive retries (no idempotency, retry=client full re-request):
- Successful sessions billed tokens = 10k * 0.92 * 300 = 2,760,000 tokens/day.
- Disconnects billed tokens = 10k * 0.08 * 120 = 96,000 tokens/day.
- If every disconnect triggers a retry that replays the full 300 tokens on retry and succeeds: additional billed tokens = 10k * 0.08 * 300 = 240,000 tokens/day.
- Total tokens/day ≈ 3,096,000 tokens.

Scenario B — idempotent + caching (cache replays for 50% of retries):
- Successful sessions = same 2,760,000 tokens/day.
- Disconnects billed tokens = same 96,000 tokens/day.
- Retries with cache hit rate 50% => additional billed tokens = 10k * 0.08 * 0.5 * 300 = 120,000 tokens/day.
- Total tokens/day ≈ 2,976,000 tokens.

Ballpark cost delta (using hosted per-token tier from the attached rate card):
- Using the rate card row for hosted generation (tiered): assume $0.0005 per token for rough math.
- Scenario A daily spend ≈ $1,548/day.
- Scenario B daily spend ≈ $1,488/day.
- Delta ≈ $60/day (~4% savings) for the given parameters; savings scale with prompt length and disconnect rate.

Discounts and pilot pricing:
- For pilots of this size we can offer a one-time 15% pilot credit on usage, applied retroactively for the pilot period (subject to a short pilot MSA).
- For committed contracts we can discuss standard committed-use discounts (volume tiers + term). I’ve linked the provisional pricing in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-9876

Operational notes:
- We emit per-request billing events in the Console (token counts + per-route breakdown). We can add a request id to the analytics view if you want to correlate; Diego can take that as a scoped engineering request.
- Throttling: streaming uses per-connection soft limits; we'll share recommended client backoff knobs — typically you won’t hit them at your pilot scale.

If that looks good I’ll have Contracts prepare a pilot addendum and Marissa can coordinate next steps.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
